newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mayor held in corruption probes resigns.
newsitem.headline: French mayor held in corruption probes resigns.

text.p: The jailed mayor of the chic French Riviera resort of Cannes, Michel Mouillot, resigned on Thursday, a week after the Supreme Court threw out an appeal against his conviction for sleaze.

Once dubbed the "Kennedy of the Croisette", the centre-right politician was barred from holding public office for five years as part of an 18-month suspended prison sentence and 200,000 franc ($40,000) fine for receiving a ficticious salary from a Lyon businessman.
He has been in pre-trial custody since last July for two other corruption cases in which he is accused of having solicited bribes in exchange for permits to install one-arm bandits in casinos.

An investigating judge placed billionaire Swiss businessman Nessim Gaon under investigation on Tuesday on suspicion of ordering payment of a 1.45 million franc ($290,000) bribe to Mouillot in return for a permit to put 100 extra slot machines in the Grand Riviera Casino in his Cannes Noga-Hilton hotel.
Gaon, 76, who is father-in-law of Joel Herzog, the son of former Israeli president Haim Herzog, was released on bail.
Joel Herzog, a director of Gaon's Noga group, is in custody in the same case.
The other case involves a casino owned by a British gambling company.
Former diplomat Maurice Delaunay, 77, who has been acting mayor since Mouillot was arrested last July, is expected to be elected in his place by the town council.
